title: Cherry Pickup II
summary: Given a grid of cherries, two robots start at opposite corners.
statement: Given a grid of cherries, two robots start at opposite corners. Each can move to adjacent cells or stay in place. They must collect cherries by moving down the grid, picking up all cherries in a cell, and avoiding overlap unless both are in the same cell. The goal is to maximize the total cherries collected by both robots by the time they reach the bottom row.
constraints: Two robots start at row zero columns zero and last; each moves to column-1, same, or column+1 on the next row.
Collect a cell once when both robots occupy it; maximize total through the last row.
hints: DP state after a row is the pair of robot columns and best collected total.
Try all nine legal next-column pairs.
Add both cells, but only once if columns coincide.
Every pair of robot paths has a unique prior state and next move, so row transitions enumerate all possibilities.
